summary: John Alexander Stewart worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at the University of Aberdeen (~1899–1903), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1905–1933) and held posts at the University of London (~1933–1944) and SOAS (~1933–1948).

An Indologist and historian, John Allan studied at Edinburgh (~1902–1906) and Leipzig (~1906–1907). He served at the British Museum from 1907, becoming Keeper of Coins and Medals in 1931, and taught Sanskrit at UCL, SOAS, and Edinburgh.

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst, Tübingen, Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney (~1867–1870). He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

John B. Carman was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions and held a faculty appointment at Harvard University (attested 1999).

John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago. He founded the Center for Process Studies and held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University (attested 1989).
John Berthrong worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alfonso Verdu (~1974–1979) and served on the faculty at Boston University from ~1989 to 2013.

A scholar of Indology and linguistics, John Borthwick Gilchrist studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the East India Company, headed Fort William College (1800–1804), and became the first Professor of Hindustani at UCL (~1828–1831).
John Brockington is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held a post as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (attested 1987 and 2003).

John Brough studied at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey. An Indologist and linguist, he held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, the University of London (1948–1967), and Cambridge (1967–1984).
John Buescher specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).

John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1880–1882) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1883–1887). He held a post at the University of St Andrews from ~1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at the Royal College of Music and Oxford, he held posts at Deccan College (~1951–1953), SOAS University of London (~1953–1984), and the Royal Asiatic Society (~1968–1971).
John C. Huntington was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University (attested 1987–1990 and 2000).

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of North Florida (attested 1988), where he became distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy (attested 2015).

John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1790–1797) and under Henry Thomas Colebrooke (~1803–1811). He was professor of Hindustani at Fort William College (1808) and secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1810–1811).

John Chadwick worked in linguistics and classics/archaeology, studying at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked at Oxford (~1946–1952) and Cambridge (from 1952), serving as Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics (1969–1984) and Fellow of Downing College.

John Claude White worked in Tibetology and archaeology. He studied at the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876) and was appointed Assistant Engineer in the Bengal Public Works Department in 1876.

John Clifford Holt works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus, GTU, and Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, later holding posts at Bowdoin (~1978–1988), Calgary (2006), and Chicago (~2020).

John Collinson Nesfield worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at Merton College. He taught at Presidency University (~1867–1872) and Krishnagar Government College (~1872–1874), and served as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878).

John Corrigan is a religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). He held posts at Virginia, Arizona State (~1990–2000), and Florida State University, where he chaired the Department of Religion (~2001).
